reference.title: Capsular invasion and post-FNA mimickers
reference.intro: Distinguishing true trans-capsular invasion from post-FNA artefact determines whether an encapsulated follicular-patterned tumour is benign/low-risk (adenoma, NIFTP), uncertain (FT-UMP/WDT-UMP), or invasive carcinoma.

groups.heading: Unequivocal capsular invasion
points: Requires complete, full-thickness penetration of the fibrous tumour capsule by tumour cells ("mushrooming" protrusion) or a separate tumour nest completely outside the outer edge of the capsule.
Minimally invasive FTC/IEFVPTC/oncocytic carcinoma: capsular invasion only, with no angioinvasion.
Widely invasive: extensive infiltration of the capsule and surrounding thyroid parenchyma, often grossly apparent.

images.caption: Unequivocal capsular invasion: full-thickness trans-capsular "mushrooming" protrusion (A, B) and separate satellite tumour nests beyond the fibrous capsule (C, D) (H&E).
images.credit: Dioufa et al., Virchows Archiv 2025 (PMC12876452), Fig 1

groups.heading: Mimickers of capsular invasion (post-FNA change)
points: Prior fine-needle aspiration produces a linear needle tract through the capsule with fresh haemorrhage, haemosiderin-laden macrophages, granulation tissue, fibrosis and mechanically displaced follicles.
Do not diagnose capsular invasion solely at a site showing FNA-tract reaction; examine the remainder of the capsule thoroughly.

images.caption: Mimickers of capsular invasion: reactive fibrosis, haemorrhage, haemosiderin-laden macrophages and displaced follicles along a prior fine-needle aspiration tract (H&E).
images.credit: Dioufa et al., Virchows Archiv 2025 (PMC12876452), Fig 2

groups.heading: Tumours of uncertain malignant potential (FT-UMP / WDT-UMP)
points: Reserved for encapsulated follicular-patterned tumours with questionable (incomplete or ambiguous) capsular or vascular invasion after thorough sampling and deeper levels.
FT-UMP lacks papillary-like nuclear features; WDT-UMP has well- or partially developed papillary-like nuclear features. Neither is staged as carcinoma.

reference.title: Thyroid carcinoma types (WHO 5th edition)
reference.intro: WHO 5th edition (2022) separates invasive encapsulated follicular variant PTC (IEFVPTC) from classic/infiltrative PTC, introduces differentiated high-grade thyroid carcinoma (DHGTC), and classifies pure squamous cell carcinoma of the thyroid under anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.
reference.noteTop: Subcentimetre papillary carcinomas are subtyped by the same criteria as larger tumours; "papillary microcarcinoma" is no longer a separate WHO subtype.

groups.heading: Papillary carcinoma, classic subtype
points: Well-formed papillae with fibrovascular cores lined by cells with enlarged, elongated, overlapping, optically clear nuclei, longitudinal grooves and intranuclear pseudoinclusions.
Psammoma bodies and stromal fibrosis are frequent; BRAF V600E is the predominant driver.

images.caption: Classic papillary thyroid carcinoma: enlarged, overlapping, optically clear ("Orphan Annie eye") nuclei with longitudinal nuclear grooves and intranuclear pseudoinclusions (H&E).
images.credit: Librepath

groups.heading: Aggressive papillary carcinoma subtypes (tall cell, hobnail, columnar cell)
points: Tall cell subtype (WHO 5th): >= 30% of tumour cells with height >= 3x width, abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, distinct cell borders and "tram-track" elongated follicles.
Hobnail subtype: >= 30% of cells with apically placed nuclei bulging into the lumen (loss of polarity) and micropapillary architecture.
Columnar cell subtype: prominent nuclear pseudostratification and supranuclear/subnuclear cytoplasmic vacuoles.

images.caption: Papillary carcinoma, tall cell subtype: elongated "tram-track" follicles and papillae lined by eosinophilic cells at least three times as tall as wide (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron

images.caption: Tall cell and hobnail subtypes of papillary thyroid carcinoma: elongated eosinophilic tall cells contrasted with micropapillae showing apically placed, bulging hobnail nuclei (H&E).
images.credit: Cameselle-Teijeiro, Eloy & Sobrinho-Simões (Endocr Pathol 2020)

links.label: ExpertPath: Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma, Tall Cell Variant
ExpertPath: Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma, Hobnail Variant

groups.heading: Papillary carcinoma, oncocytic classic subtype
points: Papillary architecture lined by oncocytic cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and diagnostic papillary nuclear features.
Distinguish from oncocytic (Hürthle cell) carcinoma, which lacks papillary nuclear features and is follicular-patterned.

images.caption: Papillary carcinoma, oncocytic subtype: papillae lined by tumour cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and classic papillary nuclear features (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron

groups.heading: Invasive encapsulated follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma (IEFVPTC)
points: Recognised as a separate entity from classic PTC in WHO 5th edition because it shares RAS-like biology and metastatic behaviour with follicular carcinoma.
Encapsulated follicular-patterned tumour with papillary-like nuclear features AND unequivocal capsular or vascular invasion.
Subdivided into minimally invasive (capsular invasion only), encapsulated angioinvasive, and widely invasive.

images.caption: Minimally invasive encapsulated follicular variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma (IEFVPTC): follicular-patterned encapsulated tumour with unequivocal capsular invasion and papillary-like nuclear features (H&E).
images.credit: Dioufa et al., Virchows Archiv 2025 (PMC12876452), Fig 9

links.label: ExpertPath: Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma, Follicular Variant

groups.heading: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
points: Follicular-patterned encapsulated or invasive neoplasm WITHOUT papillary-like nuclear features and WITH unequivocal capsular and/or vascular invasion.
Subdivided into minimally invasive (capsular invasion only), encapsulated angioinvasive (count blood vessels: < 4 vs >= 4), and widely invasive.

images.caption: Follicular thyroid carcinoma: follicular-patterned tumour lacking papillary-like nuclear features and invading through its fibrous capsule (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron

groups.heading: Oncocytic carcinoma of the thyroid
points: Replaces "Hürthle cell carcinoma" in WHO 5th edition: >= 75% oncocytic follicular cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, lacking papillary nuclear features.
Requires capsular and/or vascular invasion; subdivided into minimally invasive, encapsulated angioinvasive, and widely invasive.

images.caption: Oncocytic (Hürthle cell) carcinoma of the thyroid: >= 75% oncocytic follicular cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, lacking papillary nuclear features (H&E).
images.credit: Librepath

groups.heading: Differentiated high-grade (DHGTC) and poorly differentiated (PDTC) thyroid carcinoma
points: DHGTC: retains differentiated architecture/cytology (PTC, FTC or oncocytic carcinoma) with >= 5 mitoses/2 mm² and/or tumour necrosis, without anaplastic features.
PDTC (Turin criteria): solid/trabecular/insular growth, absence of conventional PTC nuclear features, and at least one of >= 3 mitoses/2 mm², tumour necrosis or convoluted nuclei.

images.caption: Differentiated high-grade thyroid carcinoma (DHGTC): retained differentiated cytomorphology with trabecular/solid areas and extensive coagulative tumour necrosis (arrow) (H&E).
images.credit: Cochand-Priollet et al., Current Oncology 2023 (PMC10453903), Fig 6

images.caption: Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma (PDTC): solid/insular growth pattern with capsular invasion and loss of conventional papillary nuclear features (H&E).
images.credit: Dioufa et al., Virchows Archiv 2025 (PMC12876452), Fig 10

groups.heading: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (including squamous cell carcinoma pattern)
points: Undifferentiated follicular cell-derived carcinoma composed of pleomorphic epithelioid, spindle, giant or squamoid cells; PAX8 is retained in ~50–70% while TTF-1 and thyroglobulin are usually lost.

WHO 5th edition classifies pure squamous cell carcinoma of the thyroid under anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (always staged as pT4 unless a minor/focal component without ETE — check BRAF V600E urgently).

images.caption: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma: sheets of markedly pleomorphic, undifferentiated epithelioid and spindle cells with high mitotic activity and infiltrative growth (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron

images.caption: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma pattern: cohesive sheets and ribbons of malignant squamous cells; classified under ATC in WHO 5th edition (H&E).
images.credit: Cochand-Priollet et al., Current Oncology 2023 (PMC10453903), Fig 8

groups.heading: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
points: C-cell-derived neuroendocrine carcinoma: nests/sheets of round, plasmacytoid or spindle cells with salt-and-pepper chromatin and frequent stromal amyloid.
Positive for calcitonin, CEA, chromogranin, synaptophysin and INSM1; negative for thyroglobulin. Always grade using IMTCGS.

images.caption: Medullary thyroid carcinoma: nests of round to plasmacytoid neuroendocrine cells with salt-and-pepper chromatin set in eosinophilic amyloid stroma (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron

groups.heading: Non-invasive follicular thyroid neoplasm with papillary-like nuclear features (NIFTP)
points: Low-risk follicular-patterned neoplasm (not staged by pTNM): well-demarcated/encapsulated, nuclear score 2–3, < 1% true papillae, no psammoma bodies, no capsular or vascular invasion, no tumour necrosis, and < 3 mitoses/2 mm².
Requires submission of the entire tumour-to-capsule interface to exclude invasion.

images.caption: Non-invasive follicular thyroid neoplasm with papillary-like nuclear features (NIFTP): well-demarcated follicular-patterned nodule with papillary-like nuclei and an intact capsule with no invasion (H&E).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström

fields.label: Mitotic count (per 2 mm²)
options: Greater than or equal to 3 but less than 5 mitoses per 2 mm²
Greater than or equal to 5 mitoses per 2 mm²
fields.help: Hot spot count per 2 mm² (using a 22 mm eyepiece at 40x objective, ~8.4 HPF = 2 mm²). >= 5 mitoses/2 mm² defines DHGTC in differentiated carcinomas and high-grade MTC.

reference.title: High-grade features: DHGTC, PDTC and IMTCGS
reference.intro: WHO 5th edition requires mitotic counting per 2 mm² in a hot spot (~8.4 HPF with a 22 mm eyepiece at 40x objective) plus evaluation of coagulative tumour necrosis (and Ki-67 in medullary carcinoma).

groups.heading: Differentiated high-grade thyroid carcinoma (DHGTC)
points: Retains differentiated architecture/cytology of PTC, FTC or oncocytic carcinoma.
Defined by >= 5 mitoses per 2 mm² AND/OR coagulative tumour necrosis (exclude post-FNA infarction/degeneration).
No anaplastic (undifferentiated) component.

images.caption: Differentiated high-grade thyroid carcinoma (DHGTC): retained differentiated cytomorphology with trabecular/solid areas and extensive coagulative tumour necrosis (arrow) (H&E).
images.credit: Cochand-Priollet et al., Current Oncology 2023 (PMC10453903), Fig 6

groups.heading: Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma (PDTC — Turin criteria)
points: Solid, trabecular or insular growth pattern in a follicular cell-derived invasive carcinoma.
Absence of conventional nuclear features of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
At least ONE of: >= 3 mitoses per 2 mm², tumour necrosis, or convoluted nuclei.

images.caption: Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma (PDTC): solid/insular growth pattern with capsular invasion and loss of conventional papillary nuclear features (H&E).
images.credit: Dioufa et al., Virchows Archiv 2025 (PMC12876452), Fig 10

groups.heading: High-grade medullary thyroid carcinoma (IMTCGS)
points: International Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma Grading System (WHO 5th edition): two-tiered (low grade vs high grade).
High grade if ANY ONE of the following is present: >= 5 mitoses per 2 mm², tumour necrosis, or Ki-67 labelling index >= 5% (count >= 500 tumour cells in a hot spot).

images.caption: High-grade medullary thyroid carcinoma: easily identified mitotic figures (arrows) in a hot spot; >= 5 mitoses per 2 mm² defines high grade under IMTCGS (H&E).
images.credit: Cochand-Priollet et al., Current Oncology 2023 (PMC10453903), Fig 10

images.caption: High-grade medullary thyroid carcinoma (IMTCGS): coagulative tumour necrosis (A, H&E), frequent mitotic figures (B, H&E), and elevated Ki-67 labelling index >= 5% (C, Ki-67 immunostain).
images.credit: Goswami et al., Journal of Medicine and Life 2024 (PMC11080517), Fig 7

fields.label: Angioinvasion (blood vessel invasion)
fields.help: CAP 4.4.0.0 separates blood vessel invasion (angioinvasion) from lymphatic invasion; >= 4 vessels is extensive angioinvasion.

reference.title: Angioinvasion vs lymphatic invasion (CAP 4.4.0.0)
reference.intro: CAP Thyroid 4.4.0.0 and WHO 5th edition separate blood vessel invasion (angioinvasion) from lymphatic invasion because extensive angioinvasion (>= 4 vessels) independently predicts distant haematogenous metastasis.

groups.heading: True angioinvasion (blood vessel invasion)
points: Tumour cells within a blood vessel located in the tumour capsule or immediately beyond it (intratumoural vessels do not count).

Must show attachment to the vessel wall, fibrin thrombus formation, or covering by endothelial cells (CD31/ERG can confirm endothelial wrapping; free-floating tumour fragments in a lumen are artefact).

images.caption: True angioinvasion: tumour thrombus attached to the wall of an intracapsular blood vessel (A, H&E), enveloped by endothelial cells (B, endothelial immunostain) and confirmed as thyroid tumour (C, immunostain).
images.credit: Dioufa et al., Virchows Archiv 2025 (PMC12876452), Fig 3

groups.heading: Extent of angioinvasion: focal (< 4) vs extensive (>= 4)
points: Count separate foci of blood vessel invasion across all submitted sections of the tumour capsule and peritumoural tissue.
Focal angioinvasion: < 4 involved blood vessels. Extensive angioinvasion: >= 4 involved blood vessels (high-risk feature in ATA risk stratification).

groups.heading: Lymphatic invasion (report separately)
points: Tumour plugs and/or psammoma bodies inside thin-walled, D2-40-positive lymphatic channels without a muscular wall or fibrin thrombus.
Common in classic and diffuse sclerosing PTC; correlates with nodal spread rather than haematogenous metastasis and must NOT be counted towards the angioinvasion vessel count.

fields.label: Extrathyroidal extension
options: Gross, invading subcutaneous soft tissues, larynx, trachea, oesophagus or recurrent laryngeal nerve
Gross, invading prevertebral fascia or encasing the carotid artery or mediastinal vessels
fields.help: AJCC 8th edition: microscopic extrathyroidal extension does not upstage to pT3b. Gross strap muscle invasion is pT3b; larynx/trachea/oesophagus/RLN/subcutaneous tissue is pT4a; prevertebral fascia/carotid/mediastinal vessels is pT4b.

reference.title: Extrathyroidal extension (AJCC 8th edition)
reference.intro: AJCC 8th edition removed microscopic extrathyroidal extension from pT3. Only gross (macroscopic/intraoperative) extrathyroidal extension upstages the primary tumour.

groups.heading: Microscopic extrathyroidal extension (does not upstage)
points: Tumour extends microscopically into perithyroidal adipose tissue or skeletal muscle without gross invasion noted by the surgeon or on macroscopy.
Pitfall: the thyroid fibrous capsule is anatomically incomplete, especially at the isthmus and anteriorly, so benign adipose tissue and skeletal muscle can lie within the gland — do not overcall ETE.
Record as "Microscopic only (perithyroidal soft tissue)"; pT remains governed by tumour size (pT1a–pT3a).

groups.heading: Gross strap muscle invasion only (pT3b)
points: Gross (macroscopically or intraoperatively evident) extension into strap muscles only (sternohyoid, sternothyroid, thyrohyoid or omohyoid) from a tumour of any size.
Correlate histology with the operative note and gross examination before assigning pT3b.

groups.heading: Gross invasion of major neck structures (pT4a)
points: Gross extension into subcutaneous soft tissues, larynx, trachea, oesophagus or recurrent laryngeal nerve from a tumour of any size.

groups.heading: Gross invasion of prevertebral fascia or great vessels (pT4b)
points: Gross extension into prevertebral fascia or encasement of the carotid artery or mediastinal vessels from a tumour of any size.

reference.note: No openly licensed thyroid extrathyroidal extension histopathology photograph was included; criteria follow AJCC 8th edition and CAP Thyroid 4.4.0.0. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

reference.title: Regional lymph node compartments and extranodal extension (AJCC 8th edition)
reference.intro: AJCC 8th edition assigns pN1a vs pN1b solely by anatomical compartment — not by deposit size or extranodal extension — while CAP 4.4.0.0 still requires reporting ENE and largest deposit size for ATA risk stratification.

groups.heading: Central compartment: level VI and level VII (pN1a)
points: Includes pretracheal, paratracheal, prelaryngeal (Delphian), perithyroidal and superior mediastinal (level VII) lymph nodes.
Any metastatic deposit in these compartments without lateral neck involvement assigns pN1a (unilateral or bilateral).

images.caption: Lymph node metastasis of papillary thyroid carcinoma: papillary fronds and colloid-filled follicles with optically clear nuclei replacing nodal lymphoid parenchyma (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron

groups.heading: Lateral neck (levels I–V) and retropharyngeal nodes (pN1b)
points: Includes unilateral, bilateral or contralateral lateral cervical nodes (levels I–V) or retropharyngeal lymph nodes.
Involvement of any lateral neck or retropharyngeal node assigns pN1b regardless of central compartment status.

groups.heading: Extranodal extension (ENE) and deposit size
points: ENE is defined as metastatic tumour extending through the lymph node capsule into perinodal adipose tissue or adjacent soft tissue, with or without a desmoplastic stromal reaction.
Record the greatest dimension of the largest metastatic deposit (mm) — ATA 2015 uses > 2 mm, > 5 involved nodes, and >= 30 mm (3 cm) deposits to stratify recurrence risk.
